published.title: Why Dividing by Zero Is Undefined
published.signature: Why is division by zero undefined in ordinary arithmetic, and why do some number systems assign it a meaning anyway? The operation a divided by 0, its relation to multiplicative inverses, and the difference between a limit that approaches a value and a value that is actually assigned. Division by b is multiplication by the reciprocal of b, and zero has no reciprocal in the real numbers; limits describe approach, not the value at the forbidden point.

pending.title: Why Is the Sky Blue? Rayleigh Scattering Explained
pending.signature: Why does a clear sky appear blue, and why does the same scattering process make a setting Sun look red or orange? The wavelength dependence of Rayleigh scattering, how it redistributes sunlight across the sky, and why the long path through the atmosphere near the horizon removes blue light from the direct solar beam. Air molecules scatter short visible wavelengths much more efficiently than long ones, roughly as the inverse fourth power of wavelength, so scattered blue light dominates the sky while transmitted red light dominates the low Sun.
